category: anonymous pomf-style file host with a JSON upload API

free_tier.stated: No account and no stated per-file cap on the page read; the upload API takes a multipart 'file' field and answers with JSON.
free_tier.notes: The homepage publishes no number for size or retention, so the free tier is recorded as unstated rather than guessed.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no cap is published on the page; 1 MiB was accepted
per_object_cap.notes: The ceiling was not found, so the field stays null. A 1 GiB push would find it.

retention.stated: unverified: no expiry is published and the upload reply carries no expiry field
retention.notes: Retention is the one fact this service does not state anywhere on the page.

egress.terms: Downloads are served from kappa.lol; no byte counter and no download counter are published.

interface_detail: POST https://kappa.lol/api/upload multipart field 'file'. JSON reply: id, ext, type, checksum (MD5), key, link, delete.
tooling: An official uploader exists at github.com/Mald-Entertainment-Studio/uploader; curl works with one multipart POST
chaining: A stored URL with no extension is a clean drop for a script that only needs a link a human can open; it pairs with a checksum check from the client side because the service returns MD5 itself.
limits_note: The page title is 'segs.lol', not the host name: the brand and the domain disagree, which is the kind of drift that breaks a hard-coded allow-list.
binding_note: No documented constraint exists to name. At 1 TiB a month nothing in the seven-value vocabulary was observed to bind, because neither a cap nor a retention limit nor a rate is published; the honest answer is that the ceiling is unmeasured, not absent.

identity_cost.detail: One multipart POST with no cookie and no account returned a link; the reply also carries a delete URL, which is the only control the uploader gets.

reliability_note: The reply URL carries no file extension (https://kappa.lol/P224n5), so a client that infers type from the URL gets application/octet-stream regardless of the real bytes.
confidence_note: Upload, read-back and SHA-256 match. The record stays at measured even though the cap and retention are unverified, because neither is claimed as a number here.

evidence.proved: POST of 1 048 576 bytes -> HTTP 200, JSON {'id':'P224n5','ext':'.bin','checksum':'0316a02c6c0e8b28ad82065de17289c4','link':'https://kappa.lol/P224n5'}; the checksum equals the MD5 of the uploaded file
read-back 1 048 576 bytes, sha256 da0099c231f1182a5d411c8ac5149dfb7a2e3578a3970928490cb78ba92aecc9, full-body hash matched
the page <title> is 'segs.lol'; no size or retention number appears on the page

notes: Useful as a one-line anonymous store, unusable as an archive until the cap and retention are measured. The absent extension in the returned URL is the practical trap: a resumption test keyed on Content-Type will see application/octet-stream for every file.
